In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PBMCs and PFMCs of human subjects infected with tuberculosis recognize a common set of low-molecular-weight polypeptide antigens from M. tuberculosis, which are different from those recognized by healthy subjects.
the peripheral blood monocytes and pleural fluid lymphocytes of tuberculous patients and healthy contacts recognize the same antigens, but the intensity of recognition varies.
the PBMCs and PFMCs of human tuberculosis subjects recognize a common panel of antigens, which may be used to develop a novel vaccine against tuberculosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the peripheral blood monocytes and the pleural fluid monocytes recognize a common set of antigens in tuberculosis, which is consistent with the notion of a common immune response in tuberculosis.
